A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of REArtGS++, with matching sections, equations, experiments and references. Both end on page 10; neither includes an appendix or the supplementary material referenced in the text. The supplied contents support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and joint-estimation experiments on synthetic and real objects, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments, ablations and qualitative reconstruction results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–7.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.6 retain the same planar Gaussian representation, decoupled screw-motion blending, temporal geometric constraint, local voting, initialization, optimization and mesh extraction.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same PARIS objects, five ArtGS-Multi objects, two additional screw-joint objects and real-world objects, including three captured by the authors. No task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PARIS, DTA, ArtGS and REArtGS as comparators. Table 2 and the qualitative comparisons retain ArtGS and REArtGS. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated Axis Pos unit from cm to mm, matching revised captions in Tables 1–3, but retains 'multiplied by 100.' This changes metric reporting without establishing a computation change or rerun. Other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, temporal-constraint variants, qualitative analyses and optimization-time comparison are retained. Tables 3–4 and Figure 6 test the same questions; the unit relabeling adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The existing averaging practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Axis Pos unit relabeling changes the reported absolute scale: the proposed method's synthetic PARIS mean is 0.45 cm in v1 and 0.45 mm in v3 (Table 1). Every numerical table entry, ranking and qualitative result is otherwise identical; this does not demonstrate a performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15 and their accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including motion blending and the Taylor-based temporal constraint. Neither supplied PDF adds a proof or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reconstruction without joint-type priors, temporal geometry constraints and superiority on synthetic and real objects.

C2.justification: The explanations of reconstruction quality, joint estimation and ablation behavior are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning transparent objects and camera-pose alignment between states.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, initialization thresholds, TSDF voxel size, RTX 4090 hardware, iteration budgets, timing estimates and the project-site link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 32 references and related-work discussion remain. Positioning relative to prior Gaussian-splatting and articulated-object reconstruction methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The author name 'Qiaoyu Jun' becomes 'Qiaojun Yu,' affiliation 4 changes from Shanghai AI Laboratory to RoboticsX, Tencent, and an internship footnote is added. Scientific prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 have revised unit captions, with caption reflow in Table 2. The additional author footnote causes limited text reflow on pages 1–2. Figures, table structures and displayed numerical entries remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and evidence are retained, alongside limited attribution updates. The consequential edit changes Axis Pos from cm to mm without changing scores or Section 5.1's 'multiplied by 100' description. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects the physical units or misstates absolute accuracy, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
